questions.question: British land revenue policies were deeply exploitative. Under which system were landlords required to pay a fixed revenue regardless of crop yield?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Zamindari**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Zamindari system was introduced by the British East India Company in 1793 through the **Permanent Settlement Act** in parts of Bengal, Bihar, and Odisha.
 
• Under this system, Zamindars (landlords) were made the owners of the land and were tasked to collect a fixed revenue from the peasants.
 
• The Zamindars had to pay a fixed amount of revenue to the British government, irrespective of the actual agricultural output or crop yield.
 
• Failure to pay the fixed revenue would result in the confiscation of the Zamindar's land by the British authorities.
 
• This system was highly exploitative, as Zamindars often extracted exorbitant rents from the farmers, leading to widespread poverty and distress among the peasantry.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Permanent Settlement Act (1793):**

 
 
• Introduced by Lord Cornwallis, it aimed to create a loyal class of landlords who would support British rule.
 
• Zamindars were recognized as the hereditary owners of the land, with the right to collect rent from peasants.
 
• The land revenue was fixed permanently, meaning it would not be increased in the future.
 
 
 
• **Ryotwari System:**
 
 
• Introduced in Madras and Bombay Presidencies by Thomas Munro and Alexander Read.
 
• Under this system, peasants (ryots) were recognized as the landowners and were directly responsible for paying land revenue to the government.
 
 
 
• **Mahalwari System:**
 
 
• Implemented in parts of North-Western Provinces, Punjab, and Central India.
 
• Revenue settlement was made collectively with a village or group of villages (mahal).
 
 
 
• **Exploitation Under Zamindari:**
 
 
• The fixed revenue often exceeded the peasant's capacity to pay, especially during famines or crop failures.
 
• The system resulted in the marginalization of peasants and the enrichment of Zamindars.

questions.question: The average weight of 14 boys in a class is 40.25 kg and that of the remaining 4 boys is 38 kg. Find the average weight (in kg, rounded off to two decimal place) of all the boys in the class.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of **number of boys** = 14 : 4 = 7 : 2.

Assume **base average** = 38 kg.

Deviation of 14 boys = 40.25 − 38 = +2.25 kg.

Total deviation = 14 × 2.25 = 31.5 kg.

Average increase = 31.5 ÷ 18 = 1.75 kg.

**Final Average** = 38 + 1.75 = 39.75 kg.

**∴ The correct answer is 39.75 kg.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Average weight** of first 14 boys = 40.25 kg

**Average weight** of remaining 4 boys = 38 kg

**Formula Used:**

Average = (Sum of all observations) ÷ (Total number of observations)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/d9059688428a78b35b029fa31eec6144b23c0f90cdc4ad58ec6e363257877fd7.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ **Total weight** of 14 boys = 14 × 40.25 = 563.5 kg

⇒ **Total weight** of 4 boys = 4 × 38 = 152 kg

⇒ **Total number of boys** = 14 + 4 = 18 boys

⇒ **Total weight** of class = 563.5 + 152 = 715.5 kg

⇒ **Required Average weight** = 715.5 ÷ 18

⇒ Average weight = 39.75 kg

**∴ The correct answer is 39.75 kg.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Weighted Average Formula

When two groups with averages A₁ and A₂ and sizes n₁ and n₂ are combined, the new average is (n₁A₁ + n₂A₂) ÷ (n₁ + n₂).

Properties of Average

If every observation is increased by a constant k, the **new average** also increases by k. The average always lies between the minimum and maximum values of the data set.

Deviation Concept

Net deviation about the average is always zero. This principle is used to solve **mixture and average** problems faster by assuming a middle value as the mean.</p

questions.question: In quadrilateral PQRS, the bisectors of ∠R and ∠S meet at point T (inside the quadrilateral), and ∠STR = 8°. If the ratio of ∠P to ∠Q is 7 : 9, then what is the difference between the measures of ∠Q and ∠P?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

The angle between the bisectors of two adjacent angles of a quadrilateral is equal to half the sum of the other two angles.

∴ ∠STR = (∠P + ∠Q) ÷ 2 ⇒ 8° = (∠P + ∠Q) ÷ 2 ⇒ ∠P + ∠Q = 16°

Given ratio of ∠P : ∠Q = 7 : 9. Sum of ratio parts = 7 + 9 = 16 units.

Since 16 units = 16°, then 1 unit = 1°.

Difference between ∠Q and ∠P = 9 − 7 = 2 units = 2°.

**∴ The correct answer is 2°.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

In quadrilateral PQRS, the bisectors of ∠R and ∠S meet at T.

∠STR = 8°

Ratio of ∠P : ∠Q = 7 : 9

**Formula Used:**

Sum of all interior angles of a quadrilateral = 360°

Sum of angles in a triangle = 180°

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/342973b192a53d07ccbdd5f1027e7efd2e2dc5b4c406fe3c7e8a993d0d8b10de.png] 

**Calculations:**

In ▵STR:

⇒ ∠STR + ∠TSR + ∠TRS = 180°

Since ST and RT are the bisectors of ∠S and ∠R respectively:

⇒ ∠TSR = ∠S ÷ 2

⇒ ∠TRS = ∠R ÷ 2

Substituting these values in the triangle angle sum equation:

⇒ 8° + (∠S ÷ 2) + (∠R ÷ 2) = 180°

⇒ (∠S + ∠R) ÷ 2 = 180° − 8°

⇒ (∠S + ∠R) ÷ 2 = 172°

⇒ ∠S + ∠R = 344°

In quadrilateral PQRS, the sum of all interior angles is 360°:

⇒ ∠P + ∠Q + ∠R + ∠S = 360°

⇒ ∠P + ∠Q + 344° = 360°

⇒ ∠P + ∠Q = 360° − 344°

⇒ ∠P + ∠Q = 16°

Given that the ratio of ∠P to ∠Q is 7 : 9, let ∠P = 7x and ∠Q = 9x:

⇒ 7x + 9x = 16°

⇒ 16x = 16°

⇒ x = 1°

Therefore, the measures of the angles are:

⇒ ∠P = 7 × 1° = 7°

⇒ ∠Q = 9 × 1° = 9°

The difference between the measures of ∠Q and ∠P is:

⇒ ∠Q − ∠P = 9° − 7° = 2°

**Option Analysis:**

• **Option (1) 0.5°:** Incorrect. If the difference were 0.5°, then 2x = 0.5° ⇒ x = 0.25°, which would mean ∠P + ∠Q = 16 × 0.25° = 4°, contradicting the given ∠STR = 8°.

• **Option (2) 4°:** Incorrect. If the difference were 4°, then 2x = 4° ⇒ x = 2°, which would mean ∠P + ∠Q = 16 × 2° = 32°, contradicting the given ∠STR = 8°.

• **Option (3) 2°:** Correct. This value perfectly satisfies the angle sum property and the given angle bisector relation.

• **Option (4) 7°:** Incorrect. If the difference were 7°, then 2x = 7° ⇒ x = 3.5°, which would mean ∠P + ∠Q = 16 × 3.5° = 56°, contradicting the given ∠STR = 8°.

**∴ The correct answer is 2°.**

**__Additional Information__**

Angle Bisector Theorem in Quadrilaterals

The angle formed by the bisectors of two adjacent angles of a quadrilateral is equal to half the sum of the remaining two angles: ∠STR = (∠P + ∠Q) ÷ 2.

Sum of Interior Angles of a Polygon

For any n-sided polygon, the sum of interior angles is given by (n − 2) × 180°. For a quadrilateral (n = 4), the sum is 360°.

Opposite Angle Bisectors

The angle between the bisectors of two opposite angles of a quadrilateral is equal to half the difference of the other two angles.</p

questions.question: If a² + b² =179 and a × b = 14, then find ((a-b))/((a+b)) , where a > 1
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

To find the value of (a − b) / (a + b)² based on the given options, we first find the squares.

**(a − b)²** = (a² + b²) − 2ab = 179 − 2(14) = 151 ⇒ **(a − b)** = √151.

**(a + b)²** = (a² + b²) + 2ab = 179 + 2(14) = 179 + 28 = 207.

Combining these to match the required format: (a − b) / 207 = √151 / 207.

**∴ The correct answer is √151/207.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

a² + b² = 179

ab = 14

**Formula Used:**

(a − b)² = a² + b² − 2ab

(a + b)² = a² + b² + 2ab

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/86bea0160907776727706bc79093391f61802e11e54fba16d4aa5f19e7c99c90.png] 

**Step-by-step Calculation:**

⇒ (a − b)² = 179 − 2 × 14

⇒ (a − b)² = 179 − 28 = 151

⇒ a − b = √151

⇒ (a + b)² = 179 + 2 × 14

⇒ (a + b)² = 179 + 28 = 207

⇒ Using the numerator **(a − b)** and denominator **(a + b)²** to match the target value:

⇒ Result = √151 / 207

**∴ The correct answer is √151/207.**

**__Additional Information__**

Algebraic Identities

The square of the sum is (a + b)² = a² + b² + 2ab and the square of the difference is (a − b)² = a² + b² − 2ab.

Relationship between Identities

The relationship between the sum and difference squares is given by (a + b)² − (a − b)² = 4ab.

Square Root Properties

For any positive number n, √n is the value which when multiplied by itself gives n. If n is not a perfect square, it is kept in surd form.</p

questions.question: Which of the following numbers is divisible by 12?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

A number is divisible by **12** if it is divisible by both **3** and **4**.

Divisibility by **4**: Last two digits must be divisible by 4 (Eliminates option 4).

Divisibility by **3**: Sum of digits must be divisible by 3.

For **2184**: 2 + 1 + 8 + 4 = 15 (Divisible by 3).

**∴ The correct answer is 2184.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Numbers (1) 2184, (2) 2800, (3) 1264, (4) 2349.

**Formula:** Divisibility by 12 ⇒ Divisibility by **co-prime factors** 3 and 4.

⇒ Checking **2184**: Last two digits are 84. 84 ÷ 4 = 21 (Divisible by 4).

⇒ Sum of digits of 2184 = 2 + 1 + 8 + 4 = 15. 15 ÷ 3 = 5 (Divisible by 3).

⇒ Checking **2800**: Sum = 2 + 8 + 0 + 0 = 10 (Not divisible by 3).

⇒ Checking **1264**: Sum = 1 + 2 + 6 + 4 = 13 (Not divisible by 3).

⇒ Checking **2349**: Last digit is odd (Not divisible by 4).

**∴ The correct answer is 2184.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Divisibility Rule of 3

A number is divisible by 3 if the **sum of its digits** is a multiple of 3.

Divisibility Rule of 4

A number is divisible by 4 if the **last two digits** are divisible by 4 or are double zeros (00).

Composite Divisibility

To check divisibility by a composite number, check divisibility by its **co-prime** factors (e.g., 6 = 2 × 3, 15 = 3 × 5).</p

questions.question: A car covers a distance of 1032 km in 8 hours. The speed of a train is double the speed of the car. One-third the speed of the train is equal to the speed of a bike. How much distance will the bike cover in 17 hours?

**Speed of Train** = 2 × 129 = 258 kmph.

questions.question: Five times the present age of Vashnavi is 18 years more than seven times the present age of Sooraj, and eight times the present age of Sooraj is 17 years less than five times the present age of Vashnavi. What is the sum of the present ages (in years) of Vashnavi and Sooraj?

[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let **V** be Vashnavi age and **S** be Sooraj age.

From given: 5V − 7S = 18 and 5V − 8S = 17.

Subtracting the equations: (5V − 7S) − (5V − 8S) = 18 − 17 ⇒ S = 1.

Substitute S = 1 in 5V − 8S = 17 ⇒ 5V − 8 = 17 ⇒ 5V = 25 ⇒ V = 5.

Sum of ages = 5 + 1 = 6 years.

**∴ The correct answer is 6 years.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

5 × **Vashnavi age** = 7 × **Sooraj age** + 18

8 × **Sooraj age** = 5 × **Vashnavi age** − 17

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let Vashnavi age be **V** and Sooraj age be **S**.

⇒ 5V = 7S + 18 --- (i)

⇒ 8S = 5V − 17 --- (ii)

⇒ Substitute 5V from (i) into (ii):

⇒ 8S = (7S + 18) − 17

⇒ 8S = 7S + 1

⇒ **S = 1 year**

⇒ Put S = 1 in (i): 5V = 7(1) + 18

⇒ 5V = 25 ⇒ **V = 5 years**

⇒ Sum = V + S = 5 + 1 = 6 years.

**∴ The correct answer is 6 years.**

questions.question: The least number which, when diminished by 7, is divisible by 16, 20, 10 and 27 is:

Step 1: Find prime factors of each number:

⇒ 16 = 2⁴

⇒ 20 = 2² × 5

⇒ 10 = 2 × 5

⇒ 27 = 3³

Step 2: Calculate LCM by taking highest powers of all prime factors:

⇒ LCM = 16 × 27 × 5

⇒ LCM = 432 × 5 = 2160

LCM (Least Common Multiple)

The smallest positive integer that is **perfectly divisible** by a given set of numbers.

Diminished vs Increased Logic

If a number is **diminished** by 'x', add 'x' to the LCM. If it is **increased** by 'x', subtract 'x' from the LCM.

Divisibility by 27

A number is divisible by **27** if the sum of its digits (in a specific weighted manner) or the number itself is a multiple of 27.</p

Let **a = 0.54** and **b = 0.46**. Observe that **a + b = 0.54 + 0.46 = 1**.

Using the identity **a³ + b³ = (a + b)(a² − ab + b²)**, where the sum factor is **1**.

⇒ 0.54 × 0.54 = 0.2916

⇒ 0.46 × 0.46 = 0.2116

⇒ Value = 0.157464 + 0.097336

⇒ Value = **0.2548**

**∴ The correct answer is 0.2548.**

**__Additional Information__**

Algebraic Identity for Sum of Cubes

The formula is **a³ + b³ = (a + b)(a² − ab + b²)**. This is very useful when **a + b** results in a simple integer like 1 or 10.

Algebraic Identity for Difference of Cubes

The formula is **a³ − b³ = (a − b)(a² + ab + b²)**, which is the counterpart for subtraction of cubic terms.

questions.question: Hari travels from City A to City B. If Hari drives his car at 1/4 of his normal speed, then he reaches City B 39 minutes late. Find the time (in minutes) that Hari would take to travel from City A to City B if he drove at his normal speed.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__
**Speed Ratio** (Normal : New) = 4 : 1

**Time Ratio** (Normal : New) = 1 : 4 (Since Time ∝ 1/Speed for constant distance)

Difference in time units = 4 − 1 = 3 units

Given difference = 39 minutes ⇒ 1 unit = 39 ÷ 3 = 13 minutes

**Normal Time** (1 unit) = 13 minutes

**∴ The correct answer is 13 minutes.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/05d8249cbc308d3a6123d13da5341c19971779385cc493a5f675745aa5a00e3e.png] 
**Given:**

Normal speed = S, New speed = S/4

Time difference (Δt) = 39 minutes

**Formula Used:**

Time = Distance ÷ Speed

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let normal time be T. Then new time = T + 39

⇒ Since Distance is constant, S₁ × T₁ = S₂ × T₂

⇒ S × T = (S/4) × (T + 39)

⇒ 4T = T + 39

⇒ 3T = 39

⇒ T = 13 minutes

**∴ The correct answer is 13 minutes.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Inverse Proportion of Speed and Time

When the **distance** is constant, the time taken is inversely proportional to the speed (T ∝ 1/S). If speed becomes 1/n times, time becomes n times.

Late/Early Concept Formula

Distance = [ (S₁ × S₂) / |S₁ − S₂| ] × Difference in time. This is useful for finding the actual distance between two points.</p

questions.question: The temperatures recorded over five consecutive days in a town were: 28°C, 30°C, 32°C, 31°C, and 29°C. What was the average temperature during these five days?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Assume a **base temperature** of 30°C.

Find the **deviations** from 30: (28−30), (30−30), (32−30), (31−30), (29−30) → −2, 0, +2, +1, −1.

Net deviation = (−2) + 0 + (+2) + (+1) + (−1) = 0.

Average = Base + (Net Deviation ÷ Total Days) = 30 + (0 ÷ 5) = 30°C.

**∴ The correct answer is 30°C.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Recorded temperatures for **5 consecutive days** are 28°C, 30°C, 32°C, 31°C, and 29°C.

**Formula Used:** Average = (Sum of all observations) ÷ (Number of observations)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/0a94a80a9b8cc7573de0d1901f130e5cd919d357868afeb92f30d04c0446744f.png] 

⇒ Sum of temperatures = 28 + 30 + 32 + 31 + 29

⇒ Sum = 150°C

⇒ Number of days = 5

⇒ Average = 150 ÷ 5

⇒ Average = 30°C

**∴ The correct answer is 30°C.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Arithmetic Mean Property

The algebraic sum of the **deviations** of a set of values from their arithmetic mean is always zero.

Effect of Change in Origin

If a constant value 'k' is added to or subtracted from every observation, the **new average** will also be increased or decreased by 'k'.

Weighted Average

When observations have different levels of importance, the average is calculated as Σwx ÷ Σw, where 'w' is the **weight** assigned to each value 'x'.</p

questions.question: If (x + 1/x) = 9 then (x² + 1/x²) is :
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

If the value of **x + 1/x = k**, then the value of **x² + 1/x² = k² − 2**.

In this question, **k = 9**.

∴ **x² + 1/x² = 9² − 2**

⇒ **81 − 2 = 79**

**∴ The correct answer is 79.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

The value of **x + 1/x = 9**.

**Formula Used:**

We use the **algebraic identity**: **(a + b)² = a² + b² + 2ab**

**Calculations:**

Squaring both sides of the given equation:

⇒ **(x + 1/x)² = 9²**

⇒ **x² + (1/x)² + 2 × x × (1/x) = 81**

⇒ **x² + 1/x² + 2 = 81**

⇒ **x² + 1/x² = 81 − 2**

⇒ **x² + 1/x² = 79**

**∴ The correct answer is 79.**

**__Additional Information__**

Algebraic Identity for Cubes

If **x + 1/x = k**, then the value of **x³ + 1/x³ = k³ − 3k**.

Subtraction Identity

If **x − 1/x = k**, then the value of **x² + 1/x² = k² + 2**.

Higher Power (Power of 4)

To find **x⁴ + 1/x⁴**, take the result of **x² + 1/x²** (say m), then calculate **m² − 2**.</p

• The Kanvas replaced the Shunga Dynasty in Magadha around 73 BCE after the assassination of the last Shunga ruler, Devabhuti, by his minister Vasudeva Kanva.

• The Kanva Dynasty ruled for approximately 45 years, with four rulers: Vasudeva, Bhumimitra, Narayana, and Susharman.
 
• The Kanvas were eventually overthrown by the Satavahanas, who expanded their influence in the Deccan and northern India.

• They were known for their patronage of art, including the construction of the Bharhut and Sanchi Stupas.
 
• The dynasty was marked by internal rebellions and external threats, leading to its eventual decline.
 
 
 
• **Satavahana Dynasty:**
 
 
• The Satavahanas succeeded the Kanva Dynasty and ruled large parts of central and southern India.
 
• They were known for their contributions to trade, art, and architecture, including the Amaravati Stupa.

questions.question: Which of the following materials is most suitable for making filaments in electric bulbs?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Tungsten**__.

__
 
• **Tungsten** is the most suitable material for making electric bulb filaments due to its **high melting point** of approximately 3422°C, which allows it to operate at high temperatures without melting.
 
• It has a very low rate of evaporation at high temperatures, ensuring a longer lifespan of the filament.
 
• Tungsten has excellent tensile strength, which prevents it from breaking easily when subjected to thermal expansion and contraction.
 
• Its high resistivity enables it to convert electrical energy into heat efficiently, producing bright light.
 
• When used in an inert gas-filled bulb, tungsten's performance is further enhanced by reducing filament evaporation and improving efficiency.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Properties of Tungsten:**

 
 
• The high melting point of tungsten makes it suitable for applications requiring heat resistance.
 
• Its density is around 19.3 g/cm³, making it one of the heaviest metals.
 
• Tungsten's low vapor pressure at high temperatures ensures minimal material loss.
 
 
 
• **Why Other Materials Are Not Suitable:**
 
 
• **Copper:** Low melting point (~1085°C) makes it unsuitable for high-temperature applications like filaments.
 
• **Aluminium:** Melts at approximately 660°C and lacks the durability required for filaments.
 
• **Iron:** Melting point (~1538°C) is higher than copper or aluminium but still insufficient compared to tungsten.
 
 
 
• **Inert Gas in Bulbs:** Modern electric bulbs are filled with inert gases like argon or a mixture of argon and nitrogen to prevent the oxidation of the tungsten filament and reduce evaporation.
 
• **Historical Background:** The use of tungsten in filaments was pioneered in the early 20th century, replacing earlier materials like carbon due to its superior properties.
 
• **Applications Beyond Bulbs:** Tungsten is also used in x-ray tubes, welding electrodes, and aerospace due to its heat-resistant properties.

questions.question: Find the roots of the equation 5x² - 11x + 2 = 0 by factorisation method.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For the equation 5x² − 11x + 2 = 0, find two numbers whose **product** is 10 (5 × 2) and **sum** is −11.

The required numbers are −10 and −1.

To find the roots directly, divide these factors by the coefficient of x² (which is 5) and **reverse the signs**.

Roots = −(−10 ÷ 5) = 2 and −(−1 ÷ 5) = 1/5.

**∴ The correct answer is 1/5, 2.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given Equation:** 5x² − 11x + 2 = 0

In the **factorisation method**, we split the middle term (−11x) into two terms such that their sum is −11x and their product is (5x²) × 2 = 10x².

⇒ 5x² − 10x − x + 2 = 0

⇒ 5x(x − 2) − 1(x − 2) = 0

⇒ (5x − 1)(x − 2) = 0

Now, set each factor to zero to find the roots:

⇒ 5x − 1 = 0

⇒ 5x = 1

⇒ x = 1/5

And,

⇒ x − 2 = 0

⇒ x = 2

**∴ The correct answer is 1/5, 2.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Discriminant (D)

The term D = b² − 4ac determines the nature of roots. If D > 0, roots are real and distinct; if D = 0, roots are real and equal; if D < 0, roots are imaginary.

Quadratic Formula

Roots can also be found using x = (−b ± √D) ÷ 2a.

Sum and Product of Roots

For ax² + bx + c = 0, the sum of roots is −b/a and the product of roots is c/a.</p

questions.question: In the three-tier structure of the Panchayati Raj system in India, which body is elected at the grassroots level?

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

questions.question: A grocer marked his goods at 60% above their cost price and sold them at a discount of X%. If he gained 52% profit, then find the value of X.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Successive percentage formula: **Net Change = a + b + (a × b) ÷ 100**.

Here, Markup (a) = 60%, Discount (b) = −X%, and Net Profit = 52%.

52 = 60 − X + (60 × −X) ÷ 100

52 − 60 = −X − 0.6X ⇒ −8 = −1.6X

X = 8 ÷ 1.6 = 5.

**∴ The correct answer is 5.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Let **Cost Price (CP)** = 100.
Formulas: **MP = CP × (100 + Markup%) ÷ 100** | **SP = CP × (100 + Profit%) ÷ 100** | **Discount% = (MP − SP) ÷ MP × 100**.
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/d304ef3607a0fef49a3f13d987c751699d15991af5c406c15353cc8d98d3e130.png] 
⇒ Given **Markup = 60%**, so **Marked Price (MP)** = 100 + 60 = 160.
⇒ Given **Profit = 52%**, so **Selling Price (SP)** = 100 + 52 = 152.
⇒ **Discount Amount** = MP − SP = 160 − 152 = 8.
⇒ **Discount% (X)** = (8 ÷ 160) × 100.
⇒ X = (1 ÷ 20) × 100 = 5%.

**∴ The correct answer is 5.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Marked Price and Discount

The price printed on an item is the **Marked Price (MP)**. Discount is always calculated on the MP to reach the **Selling Price (SP)**.

Markup Percentage

The extra price added to the **Cost Price (CP)** to set the MP is the markup. **Markup% = [(MP − CP) ÷ CP] × 100**.</p

questions.question: A pipe can fill a tank in 8 hours. Another pipe can empty the filled tank in 16 hours. If both the pipes are opened simultaneously, then the time (in hours) in which the tank will be three-fourth filled, is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Net efficiency = **Filling rate** − **Emptying rate**.

Let **Total capacity** (LCM of 8 and 16) = 16 units.

Filling pipe efficiency = 16 ÷ 8 = 2; Emptying pipe efficiency = 16 ÷ 16 = 1.

Combined efficiency = 2 − 1 = 1 unit/hour.

Time for 3/4 filled = (3/4 × 16) ÷ 1 = 12 hours.

**∴ The correct answer is 12 hours.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Filling time = 8 hours, Emptying time = 16 hours.

**Formula Used:** Work = Efficiency × Time; Net Efficiency = (1/Filling time) − (1/Emptying time).

 
 **Pipe Type** **Time (hrs)** **Total Capacity (LCM)** **Efficiency** 
 Filling Pipe 8 16 units +2 
 Emptying Pipe 16 −1 

⇒ **Combined efficiency** of both pipes = 2 − 1 = 1 unit/hour.

⇒ Target volume to be filled = 3/4 × Total Capacity

⇒ Target volume = 3/4 × 16 = 12 units.

⇒ Time taken = Target volume ÷ Combined efficiency

⇒ Time taken = 12 ÷ 1 = 12 hours.

**∴ The correct answer is 12 hours.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Pipes and Cisterns Concept

Filling pipes (inlets) have **positive efficiency**, while emptying pipes (outlets) have **negative efficiency**.

Net Work Formula

If pipe A fills in 'x' hours and pipe B empties in 'y' hours, net work in 1 hour = (1/x − 1/y). If x < y, the tank will eventually fill.

Fractional Filling

To find time for a specific fraction of the tank, multiply the total fill time by that **fractional value**.</p

questions.question: If A's salary is 51% more than that of B, then by what percentage is B's salary less than that of A (correct to two decimal places)?

⇒ **A's salary** = 100 + 51% of 100 = 100 + 51 = 151

**Calculations:**

Difference between **A** and **B** = 151 − 100 = 51

Percentage by which **B** is less than **A** = (Difference / **A's salary**) × 100

⇒ Required % = (51 / 151) × 100

Percentage is always calculated relative to the **base value**. When finding 'less than A', **A's value** becomes the denominator.

Inverse Case

If A is x% less than B, then B is [x / (100 − x)] × 100% more than A.</p

questions.question: The median of the observations 85, 62, 20, 72, 20, 43, 35, 90, 68, 56 and 79 is:
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Arrange the **11 observations** in ascending order:

20, 20, 35, 43, 56, **62**, 68, 72, 79, 85, 90

Since the number of terms (N = 11) is odd, the median is the middle term:

Median = ((N + 1) ÷ 2)th term = 6th term = **62**

**∴ The correct answer is 62.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Observations: 85, 62, 20, 72, 20, 43, 35, 90, 68, 56, 79

Total number of observations (N) = 11

**Formula Used:**

When N is odd, **Median** = ((N + 1) ÷ 2)th observation after arranging in ascending order.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/bde88f3aae19202cd42664ed333510508e55725b3858b610382f208da5744016.png] 

**Calculations:**

Arrange the given observations in **ascending order**:

⇒ 20, 20, 35, 43, 56, 62, 68, 72, 79, 85, 90

Count the total number of observations:

⇒ N = 11

Since N is an **odd number**, the median is calculated as:

⇒ Median = ((11 + 1) ÷ 2)th term

⇒ Median = (12 ÷ 2)th term

⇒ Median = 6th term

Looking at the arranged sequence, the 6th term is **62**.

Let us verify why the other options are incorrect:

⇒ Option (1) 68 is the 7th term, which is not the middle term.

⇒ Option (3) 56 is the 5th term, which is not the middle term.

⇒ Option (4) 72 is the 8th term, which is not the middle term.

**∴ The correct answer is 62.**

**__Additional Information__**

Median for Even Number of Terms

If N is even, the median is the average of the (N ÷ 2)th term and the ((N ÷ 2) + 1)th term. Formula: Median = [ (N/2)th term + (N/2 + 1)th term ] ÷ 2.

Mean (Arithmetic Average)

The sum of all observations divided by the total number of observations. Formula: Mean = (Sum of all observations) ÷ N.

Mode

The observation that appears most frequently in the data set. For the given data, 20 appears twice, so the mode is 20.

Empirical Relationship

The relationship between Mean, Median, and Mode for moderately skewed distributions is: Mode = 3 × Median − 2 × Mean.</p

questions.question: By selling cloth at ₹483/m, a shopkeeper loses 31%. Find the rate (in /m) at which it should be sold so as to earn a profit of 34%.

[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Loss of 31% means selling at **(100 − 31) = 69%** of CP.

Profit of 34% means selling at **(100 + 34) = 134%** of CP.

Ratio-unitary method: If 69 units = 483, then 1 unit = 483 ÷ 69 = 7.

Target Selling Price = 134 units = 134 × 7 = 938.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹938/m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Selling Price 1 (SP₁) = ₹483, Loss% = 31%, Target Profit% = 34%.

**Formulas:** CP = [SP × 100] ÷ [100 − Loss%], New SP = [CP × (100 + Profit%)] ÷ 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/b10c750b5b865d1e69a8a97c55e2402a25959d185f7f153494bcff1176b48851.png] 

⇒ **Cost Price (CP)** = (483 × 100) ÷ (100 − 31) = (483 × 100) ÷ 69 = 7 × 100 = ₹700.

⇒ **Required Selling Price (SP₂)** = [700 × (100 + 34)] ÷ 100 = 700 × 1.34 = 938.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹938/m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Cost Price & Selling Price Relationship

When the cost price is constant, the ratio of two selling prices is directly proportional to the percentage values: **SP₁/SP₂ = (100 ± P/L₁)/(100 ± P/L₂)**.

Profit and Loss Basics

Profit is earned when SP > CP, and Loss occurs when CP > SP. All percentages are calculated on the **Cost Price** unless specified otherwise.

questions.question: Which ancient civilisations flourished in the Thar Desert area about 5000 years ago?

__
 
• The Indus Valley Civilisation, also known as Harappan Civilisation, existed approximately between 3300 BCE and 1300 BCE in the northwestern regions of South Asia.
 
• It flourished in areas of modern-day Pakistan and northwest India, including the Thar Desert region.
 
• Major sites of the civilisation include Harappa, Mohenjo-Daro, Dholavira, and Kalibangan, which are all located near river systems and arid regions like the Thar Desert.

• **Key Features:** The civilisation was known for its trade networks, craft production, and script, though the script remains undeciphered.
 
• **Climate Context:** The Thar Desert region played a role in the civilisation's adaptation strategies, including water management and agriculture in semi-arid zones.
 
• **Decline:** The decline of the civilisation is attributed to environmental changes, such as the drying up of the Sarasvati River and possible shifts in monsoon patterns.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT an elected position under the Panchayati Raj system in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Panchayat Secretary**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The **Panchayat Secretary** is not an elected position under the Panchayati Raj system; it is an appointed administrative role.
 
• The Panchayat Secretary is usually appointed by the **state government** to assist in the functioning and administration of the Panchayat.
 
• This role primarily involves record-keeping, maintaining accounts, and implementing government schemes at the Panchayat level.
 
• In contrast, positions like **Sarpanch, Zila Pramukh, and Pradhan** are elected by the people under the democratic framework of the Panchayati Raj system.
 
• The Panchayat Secretary acts as a link between the elected representatives and the state government for administrative purposes.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Panchayati Raj System**

 
 
• The Panchayati Raj is a three-tier system of local self-governance in India, consisting of Gram Panchayat (village level), Block Samiti (block level), and Zila Parishad (district level).
 
• It was introduced through the **73rd Constitutional Amendment Act of 1992**.
 
• The system aims to empower rural areas with self-governance and decentralized administration.
 
• Each tier has elected representatives, ensuring grassroots democracy.
 
 
 
• **Key Elected Positions in Panchayati Raj**
 
 
• **Sarpanch:** Head of the Gram Panchayat, elected by the villagers.
 
• **Pradhan:** Chairperson of the Panchayat Samiti at the block level.
 
• **Zila Pramukh:** Head of the Zila Parishad, elected by the members of the Parishad.
 
 
 
• **Roles of Panchayat Secretary**
 
 
• Maintains records of meetings, resolutions, and accounts.

questions.question: Which of the following is a disproportionation reaction?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Cl2 + H2O → HCI + HOCI**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Disproportionation reactions involve the simultaneous oxidation and reduction of the same species within a chemical reaction.
 
• In the reaction **Cl₂ + H₂O → HCl + HOCl**, chlorine (Cl₂) undergoes disproportionation as it is both oxidized to form hypochlorous acid (HOCl) and reduced to form hydrochloric acid (HCl).
 
• The oxidation state of chlorine in Cl₂ is 0. In HCl, it is reduced to -1, and in HOCl, it is oxidized to +1.
 
• This reaction occurs naturally in water when chlorine is dissolved, and is often used in water purification and disinfection processes.
 
• Disproportionation reactions are a subset of redox reactions and are characterized by the same element undergoing both gain and loss of electrons.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Oxidation:** It refers to the loss of electrons or an increase in oxidation state during a chemical reaction.
 
• **Reduction:** Reduction is the gain of electrons or a decrease in oxidation state during a chemical reaction.
 
• **Oxidation State:** It is a number assigned to an element in a compound or ion that represents the number of electrons lost (positive oxidation state) or gained (negative oxidation state).
 
• **Redox Reactions:** These are reactions in which oxidation and reduction occur simultaneously, involving the transfer of electrons between species.
 
• **Applications of Disproportionation Reactions:** Such reactions are widely used in industrial processes, water treatment, and chemical synthesis (e.g., the production of bleaching agents and disinfectants).

questions.question: In what time (in years) will ₹2,800 fetch an interest of ₹700 at 5% per year simple interest?

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Principal (P) = ₹2,800

Interest (I) = ₹700

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/9f28ffa8b4fcb28db901fe241092dbe7b397002c944c21d5cdc3780d1ad412d4.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ T = (700 × 100) ÷ (2800 × 5)

⇒ T = 70,000 ÷ 14,000

Simple Interest Formula

Total Amount

For a fixed **Principal** and **Rate**, **Simple Interest** is directly proportional to **Time**. If time doubles, interest also doubles.

questions.question: If the volume of a right circular cone of height 11 cm is 297π cm³, find the diameter of its base.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Volume of **cone** V = (1/3)πr²h

297π = (1/3) × π × r² × 11

r² = (297 × 3) ÷ 11 = 27 × 3 = 81

r = 9 cm → **Diameter** = 2 × 9 = 18 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 18 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Height** (h) of the cone = 11 cm

**Volume** (V) of the cone = 297π cm³

**Formula Used:**

Volume of **Right Circular Cone** = (1/3)πr²h

**Diameter** (d) = 2 × **Radius** (r)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/1717f215cc9a219820e3610a3d51d38b519b3dca52310a724cb53801afbd07df.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ (1/3) × π × r² × 11 = 297π

⇒ (1/3) × r² × 11 = 297

⇒ r² × 11 = 297 × 3

⇒ r² = 891 ÷ 11

⇒ r² = 81

⇒ r = √81 = 9 cm

⇒ **Diameter** = 2 × r = 2 × 9 = 18 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 18 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Slant Height of Cone

The slant height (l) is the distance from the apex to any point on the base circumference: l = √(r² + h²).

Surface Area of Cone

Curved Surface Area (CSA) = πrl and Total Surface Area (TSA) = πr(l + r).

Volume Relation with Cylinder

The volume of a **cone** is exactly one-third the volume of a **cylinder** with the same radius and height.</p

questions.question: If at the same rate of interest, in 2 years, the simple interest is 40 and compound interest, compounded annually, is 42, then what is the principal (in)?

**Rate of Interest (R)** = [2 × (CI − SI) ÷ SI] × 100

⇒ R = [2 × (42 − 40) ÷ 40] × 100 = (4 ÷ 40) × 100 = 10%

**Principal (P)** = (SI × 100) ÷ (R × T)

⇒ P = (40 × 100) ÷ (10 × 2) = 4000 ÷ 20 = 200

**∴ The correct answer is 200.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

⇒ Difference (CI − SI) = 42 − 40 = 2

⇒ Rate of Interest (R) = (2 ÷ 20) × 100 = 10%

⇒ Since SI for 1 year is 20: 20 = (P × 10 × 1) ÷ 100

⇒ 20 = P ÷ 10

⇒ P = 20 × 10 = 200

**∴ The correct answer is 200.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Relation for 2 years

• Tribal populations benefit from reservations in education, employment, and political representation under the Fifth and Sixth Schedules of the Constitution.

questions.question: The famous building 'Qutub Minar' has been built under which style of architecture?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Mamulek Style**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Qutub Minar is an iconic monument constructed under the **Mamulek (or Mamluk) style of architecture**, which is a part of the Delhi Sultanate architectural tradition.
 
• It was commissioned by **Qutb al-Din Aibak**, the founder of the Delhi Sultanate, in 1192, and later completed by his successors.
 
• This architectural style is characterized by the use of red sandstone, intricate carvings, and calligraphic inscriptions, often incorporating Islamic motifs and verses from the Quran.
 
• The Qutub Minar is a UNESCO World Heritage Site and stands at a height of **72.5 meters**, making it one of the tallest minarets in the world built of bricks.
 
• The Mamulek style of architecture often blended Islamic and indigenous Indian elements, creating a unique fusion evident in monuments like the Qutub Minar.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Mamulek Architecture:**

 
 
• Also known as Mamluk architecture, it emerged during the reign of the Slave Dynasty (1206–1290) in India.
 
• It extensively used locally available materials like red sandstone while incorporating Islamic architectural features such as arches, domes, and minarets.
 
• Floral patterns, arabesques, and geometric designs were a hallmark of this style.
 
 
 
• **Qutub Minar Construction:**
 
 
• Qutb al-Din Aibak began its construction, but it was completed by his successor, Iltutmish.
 
• It is surrounded by several historically significant structures, including the Iron Pillar and Alai Darwaza.
 
• The minar has five distinct storeys, each marked by projecting balconies and intricate carvings.
 
 
 
• **Delhi Sultanate Architecture:**
 
 
• It refers to the architectural developments during the rule of the Delhi Sultanate (1206–1526).
 
• It includes other notable structures like the Alai Darwaza, the tomb of Iltutmish, and the Tughlaqabad Fort.
 
• This style laid the foundation for later Mughal architecture.
 
 
 
• **UNESCO World Heritage Site:**
 
 
• The Qutub Minar complex was designated as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1993.
 
• It is recognized for its historical, architectural, and cultural significance.

questions.question:
Which of the following is/are correct with respect to the outcomes of globalisation in the Indian economy?

1. The opening of the economy has led to a rapid decrease in foreign direct investment and foreign exchange reserves.

2. The post-1991 India witnessed a steep decline in its GDP on a continual basis for two decades.

3. The growth of GDP increased from 5.6% during 1980-91 to 8.2% during 2007-12.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Option 2**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Globalisation in India post-1991 brought significant changes to the Indian economy, particularly through economic liberalisation policies.
 
• Contrary to statement 1, the opening of the economy led to a **rapid increase in foreign direct investment (FDI)** and a substantial rise in foreign exchange reserves.
 
• Statement 2 is incorrect as post-1991 reforms resulted in **economic growth**. The GDP growth rate did not witness a decline but rather showed improvement over time.
 
• Statement 3 is correct, as the growth rate of GDP increased from **5.6% during 1980-91 to 8.2% during 2007-12**, reflecting the positive impact of globalisation on economic growth.
 
• The correct answer is Option 2, as only statement 3 accurately reflects the outcomes of globalisation in the Indian economy.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Globalisation:**

 
 
• Globalisation refers to the process of integration and interdependence of economies, societies, and cultures through cross-border trade, investment, and technology.
 
• It promotes free flow of goods, services, capital, and labour across international borders.
 
 
 
• **Economic Reforms of 1991:**
 
 
• India introduced economic reforms in 1991, focusing on liberalisation, privatisation, and globalisation (LPG model).
 
• These reforms aimed to address the balance of payment crisis and stimulate economic growth.
 
 
 
• **Foreign Direct Investment (FDI):**
 
 
• FDI refers to investments made by foreign entities in the productive capacity of another country.
 
• FDI inflows increased significantly in India post-1991 due to liberalised policies and the removal of trade barriers.
 
 
 
• **Foreign Exchange Reserves:**
 
 
• India’s foreign exchange reserves increased from $5.8 billion in 1991 to over $600 billion in recent years, showcasing the positive impact of globalisation.
 
 
 
• **GDP Growth Trends:**
 
 
• India’s GDP growth witnessed a steady rise post-1991 reforms, with significant contributions from sectors like IT, manufacturing, and services.
 
• Improved infrastructure, policy reforms, and increased trade partnerships played a key role in sustaining high GDP growth rates.

questions.question: Which of the following Articles of the Indian Constitution states about the duty of Union Public Service Commission to present its report annually to the President of India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is ​__**Article 323**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 323** of the Indian Constitution describes the duty of the Union Public Service Commission (UPSC) to present its annual report to the President of India.
 
• The President places this report before both Houses of Parliament, along with a memorandum explaining cases where the Commission's advice was not accepted.
 
• This provision ensures the accountability and transparency of the UPSC's functioning.
 
• The Union Public Service Commission is a constitutional body established under Part XIV of the Indian Constitution.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Union Public Service Commission (UPSC)**

 
 
• It is responsible for conducting examinations for appointments to civil services and posts under the Union Government.
 
• UPSC is one of the central recruiting agencies of India, established under Article 315 of the Constitution.
 
• The Commission consists of a chairman and other members appointed by the President of India.
 
• It functions independently to ensure unbiased recruitment for civil service positions.
 
 
 
• **Constitutional Articles Related to UPSC**
 
 
• **Article 315:** Establishment of Public Service Commissions for the Union and States.
 
• **Article 316:** Appointment and term of office of members of the UPSC.
 
• **Article 317:** Removal and suspension of members of Public Service Commissions.
 
• **Article 323:** Reports of the UPSC and their presentation to the President.
 
 
 
• **Role of UPSC**
 
 
• Conducting examinations such as the Civil Services Examination (CSE), Engineering Services Examination (ESE), and others.
 
• Advising the government on matters related to recruitment, promotions, and disciplinary actions.
 
• Ensuring merit-based selection for appointments in public services.
